name: MotorControl
description: Motor start/stop with a seal-in contact (LD parallel branch demo)

inputs.name: StartPB
inputs.comment: Start pushbutton, normally open: TRUE while pressed

inputs.name: StopPB
inputs.comment: Stop pushbutton, normally open: TRUE while pressed. The rung breaks on a press. A safety stop is wired the other way round (normally-closed button, TRUE while healthy), so that a broken wire also stops the motor.

inputs.name: Overload
inputs.comment: Overload relay: TRUE once it has tripped

outputs.name: MotorContactor
outputs.comment: Motor contactor coil. It is also the seal-in memory, as in a hard-wired relay circuit.

outputs.name: RunningLamp
outputs.comment: Lamp that follows the contactor command. It is not feedback: a real run lamp would use the contactor auxiliary contact.

rungs.comment: Start / stop with seal-in. The branch puts the Start button in parallel with the contactor's own contact: a press energises the contactor, and the contactor then holds itself on after the button is released. Stop or Overload opens the series contacts and drops it. With Start still held, releasing Stop or Overload runs the motor again; motor_start_stop shows the start-armed version that does not.

metadata.author: ZPLC Team
metadata.notes: One latch only: the contactor's own contact in parallel with Start holds the coil on. Compare motor_start_stop, which adds a start-armed condition so a held Start button never restarts the motor by itself.
